title: Asking Someone Not to Do Something

vocabulary.meaning_en: the person in charge of a building where goods are stored
vocabulary.example: The warehouse manager checks all deliveries.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a polite way to ask someone to do or not do something
vocabulary.example: Would you mind closing the door?
Food is not permitted in the computer room.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the official rules of a company
vocabulary.example: I'm afraid it's against company policy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: illegal; not allowed by the law
vocabulary.example: Parking here is against the law.
It is illegal to smoke inside public buildings in the UK.
Blocking the fire exit is dangerous.

vocabulary.meaning_en: showing clearly that you will not change your mind

vocabulary.example: Please put out the candle before you leave.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stop a fire or flame (formal)
vocabulary.example: Staff know how to extinguish a small fire.
An old heater could cause a fire.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the buildings and land of a business
vocabulary.example: Visitors must sign in when they enter the premises.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the time when you stop work to eat lunch
vocabulary.example: I take my lunch break at one o'clock.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to stay calm in a difficult situation
vocabulary.example: She kept her cool when the customer shouted.

vocabulary.meaning_en: worried because you have a lot to do
vocabulary.example: We're all under pressure this week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of work clothing that covers your body and legs

fine_lines.title: You mustn't vs Would you mind not...?
fine_lines.explanation_ar: You mustn't أمر مباشر وقوي. Would you mind not + فعل ing طلب مهذب لكنه حازم.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "You mustn't" is a strong, direct order. "Would you mind not + verb-ing?" is polite but still firm.

examples.sentence: You mustn't use your phone here.
Would you mind not using your phone here, please?

fine_lines.title: allowed vs permitted
fine_lines.explanation_ar: المعنى واحد (مسموح)، لكن permitted أكثر رسمية وتُستخدم في القواعد واللافتات.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Same meaning, but "permitted" is more formal and used in rules and signs.

examples.sentence: We're not allowed to park here.

expressions.phrase: Would you mind not doing that, please?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل تمانع ألا تفعل ذلك من فضلك؟
expressions.meaning_en: a polite way to ask someone to stop
expressions.example: Would you mind not talking so loudly, please?

expressions.phrase: I'm afraid it's against company policy.
expressions.meaning_en: used to give the rule as a reason
expressions.example: I'm afraid it's against company policy to share passwords.

expressions.meaning_en: a formal way to say it isn't allowed
expressions.example: I'm afraid eating at your desk is not permitted.

expressions.phrase: Sorry to have to ask you this, but...
expressions.meaning_ar: آسف لأنني مضطر لأن أطلب منك هذا، لكن...
expressions.example: Sorry to have to ask you this, but could you move your car?
It's OK this time, but please don't do it again.

expressions.meaning_ar: نحن نأخذ هذا الأمر بجدية كبيرة.
expressions.meaning_en: used to say a rule is important
expressions.example: Safety is important. We take this very seriously.

grammar.title: Would you mind (not) + verb-ing
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد Would you mind نضع الفعل بصيغة ing. لطلب التوقف عن شيء نضع not قبل الفعل: Would you mind not smoking here? ولاحظ أن الجواب No, not at all يعني الموافقة.
grammar.explanation_en: After "Would you mind" use verb-ing. To ask someone to stop, add "not": "Would you mind not doing that?" The answer "No, not at all" means "OK, I will".
examples: Would you mind opening the window?
Would you mind not eating at the computer?
Would you mind waiting a moment?

grammar.title: Softening with I'm afraid / Sorry to have to
grammar.explanation_ar: لجعل الرفض أو الطلب الصعب ألطف نبدأ بـ I'm afraid أو Sorry to have to ask you this, but ثم نذكر السبب.
grammar.explanation_en: To make a refusal or difficult request softer, start with "I'm afraid" or "Sorry to have to ask you this, but" and then give the reason.
examples: Sorry to have to ask you this, but you need to leave the room.
I'm afraid it's against the law.

questions.question: Complete: Would you mind not ___ that, please?
questions.explanation_ar: بعد mind يأتي الفعل بصيغة ing.

questions.question: Which word means "put out a fire" in a formal way?
Which is polite but firm?
choices: Would you mind not doing that, please?
questions.explanation_ar: Would you mind not... مهذبة وحازمة.
questions.explanation_en: "Would you mind not..." is polite but firm.

questions.question: Complete: I'm afraid it's ___ company policy.
questions.explanation_ar: against company policy = مخالف لسياسة الشركة.
questions.explanation_en: "Against company policy" means not allowed by the rules.

questions.question: "Premises" means...
questions.explanation_en: "Premises" means a company's buildings and land.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: Would you mind to close the door?
Would you mind close the door?
Would you mind closed the door?
Would you mind closing the door?

questions.question: "Keep your cool" means...
questions.explanation_ar: keep your cool = حافظ على هدوئك.

questions.question: Which phrase do you say BEFORE a difficult request?
choices: Sorry to have to ask you this, but...
questions.explanation_en: It comes before a difficult request.
